**Hydrogen – Key Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Symbol** | H | | **Standard atomic weight** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Isotopes** |

• ²H (deuterium) – stable isotope, ~0.015% natural abundance
• ³H (tritium) – radioactive, half‑life ≈12.32 yr | | **Melting point** | −259.16 °C (14 K) – solidifies only under high pressure or at very low temperatures | | **Boiling point** | −252.87 °C (20.28 K) – gaseous at standard conditions | | **Density** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ at 0 °C, 1 atm (lightest element) | | **Molar volume** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ at STP | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | | **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, meaning it releases energy when gaining an electron) | | **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | | **Heat capacity (Cp)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 298 K) | | **Specific heat ratio (γ = Cp/Cv)** | 1.41 (ideal diatomic gas) | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂), acids (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄), and fuels (e.g., H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O). | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – key in astrophysics. | | **Uses** | Fuel cell technology, rocket propellant, ammonia synthesis (Haber process), metal extraction, laboratory reagent, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents). | ### Additional Notes * **Physical State:** At room temperature and atmospheric pressure, hydrogen exists as a colorless, odorless, tasteless, non‑polar diatomic gas (H₂). * **Isotope Applications:** Deuterium is used in nuclear fusion research and as a tracer in biochemical studies; tritium is employed in self‑lighting devices and as a radioactive tracer. * **Safety:** While non‑toxic, hydrogen is highly flammable and can form explosive mixtures with air (5–75 % by volume). These properties make hydrogen unique among elements—its lightness, reactivity, and role in both chemistry and physics make it a cornerstone of modern science and industry.
